units: <cite ref="Chagigah 13b:5">Ḥag. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>מּלך שבעופות נ׳</he> the king of birds is the eagle.

<cite ref="Chullin 60b:16">Ḥull. 60ᵇ</cite> sq. (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 11:13">Lev. XI, 13</cite>) <he>נ׳ מה נ׳ וכ׳</he> the text specifies the eagle to intimate, as the eagle has no additional toe …, so all birds like him are unclean.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1:31">Y. Peah I, 15ᵈ</cite> top <he>נ׳ שהוא רחמן</he> the eagle who is kind (to his young ones); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 963:2">Yalk. Prov. 963</cite>. Mekh. Yithro, Baḥod., s. 2; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 12a:6">Snh. 12ᵃ</cite> (in a secret letter) <he>ותפשו נ׳</he> and the eagle (Roman) caught them (the messengers, v. <cite ref="N01124"><he>נְצִיב</he></cite>).—Pl. <he>נְשָׁרִים</he>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 92b:1">Ib. 92ᵇ</cite> <he>עושה להם כנפים כנ׳ וכ׳</he> he shall give them (the righteous) wings like those of the eagles, and they shall soar &c.; a. e.
